purpose: Forward signal tracking only. Each entry is a frozen fast/slow oscillator rule gated by a recent regular divergence on the SLOW oscillator. Emitting BUY/SELL records an observation; it is not a recommendation and carries no order authority.
known_limitations: The double-positive rate across the campaign (16/437 = 3.7%) exceeds the independence expectation (2.4%) only modestly; this set is NOT established as distinguishable from search noise.
Of 75 cells that passed holdout, only 21.3% stayed positive on confirmation, against a 14.2% marginal rate.
Cells are not independent: adjacent timeframes share signals, and ta_stochastic and ta_williams_r rows appear numerically identical in several cases.
No shifted-label or permutation null has been run against these survivors.
The retrospective confirmation window ends 2026-08-01, so tracking after that date is genuinely unseen data. That is the purpose of this registry.

registry.selection_rule: Cells positive on BOTH the optimizer holdout and the retrospective confirmation segment, with at least 10 trades on each. 16 of 437 eligible multi-asset cells qualified, plus the separately-run BTCUSDT RSI 30m cell.

reimplemented_logic.what: A dormant TAIndicatorAdapter.compute_values shim. It is INERT in this tree: commit 161d1af committed the real public method at ta_library.py:707, so the hasattr guard does not fire and nothing is installed. ta_momentum_fast_slow_divergence.py:635 calls the committed method directly. Shims installed this run: none. The committed tree defines both (ta_library.py:707 and __init__.py:50/:151), so neither guard fired and this run used the committed definitions unmodified.
reimplemented_logic.why: Before 161d1af the committed ta_library.py exposed only the private _compute_values, AttributeError was raised, and 14 of the 15 active cells could not be evaluated at all. The guard is kept as a regression tripwire: if the public method is ever removed again the delegation self._compute_values(frame, self._resolved(params)) -- which is what the committed body does -- is restored and reported instead of the run crashing.
reimplemented_logic.risk: If the shim were ever to fire again and _resolved were not the argument the committed public method passes, every oscillator would be computed with different parameters and every signal would silently drift from the frozen evidence.

reimplemented_logic.what: A dormant arbitra_indicator_optimizer.AtrBracketLifecycleEvaluator re-export shim. It is INERT in this tree: commit 161d1af committed the re-export (__init__.py:50 imports the class, :151 lists it in __all__), so the hasattr guard does not fire and no name is bound here. Shims installed this run: none. The committed tree defines both (ta_library.py:707 and __init__.py:50/:151), so neither guard fired and this run used the committed definitions unmodified.
reimplemented_logic.why: Before 161d1af the committed package __init__ omitted it and the committed arbitra_btcusdt_ta_momentum_fast_slow_divergence_mtf could not import against its own package. No behaviour was ever defined by the shim; only a name was bound.
reimplemented_logic.risk: None to the numbers: the exported object is the frozen class. The risk was that the committed tree was internally inconsistent, which a silent shim would conceal -- so it was reported, and its disappearance from the shim list is itself the evidence that the tree was repaired.

reimplemented_logic.what: derive_armed_state re-expresses the arming/consumption state machine of qualified_entry_pulses in order to report which divergence is currently armed on the last completed bar.
reimplemented_logic.why: qualified_entry_pulses keeps bullish_armed_at and bearish_armed_at as loop locals and returns only boolean columns, so the live armed flag cannot be read out of the frozen return value. The derivation consumes frozen inputs (the divergence event columns) and frozen outputs (long_entry / short_entry) only; it never recomputes a divergence, a pulse or an oscillator.
reimplemented_logic.risk: A drifted derivation would misreport armed state and a reader would mistake a stale arm for a live setup.

reimplemented_logic.what: The Binance REST JSON kline payload is parsed by a local adapter rather than by scripts/acquire_binance_klines.py::parse_klines.
reimplemented_logic.why: parse_klines takes a monthly ZIP archive payload (zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(payload))); the monthly archive is up to ~30 days stale and cannot serve a 30m watch. The adapter produces the identical column set and dtypes and reuses that module's COLUMNS and BAR_MINUTES.
reimplemented_logic.risk: A units mistake (the archive switched open_time to microseconds; REST is still milliseconds) would silently shift every bar.

reimplemented_logic.what: The lifecycle evaluator is replayed over ONE unbroken segment from the anchor, where the frozen campaign evaluated BOUNDED windows (arbitra_multi_asset_ta_oscillator_fast_slow_divergence_mtf.py:723-726, start = min(len(frame), max(plan.holdout_start, warmup))). The window is selected by replay_start_policy, emitted per cell, and defaults to 'anchor' -- the whole-history behaviour every record already in the ledger was produced under.
reimplemented_logic.why: Live tracking has no holdout boundary to start at, and moving the replay start would change signals, fills and exits that have already been published. replay_start_policy decides where the frozen lifecycle evaluator is started, and it is a scientific choice a human must make, not an optimisation. 'anchor' (the default, and the behaviour every record already in the ledger was produced under) replays one unbroken segment from the first structurally evaluable bar after ANCHOR_START_UTC=2023-03-25, so a position opened before the tracking boundary is carried across it and today's reported state depends on bars from 2023; it also costs O(whole history) on every tick. 'tracking_start' reproduces what the frozen campaign actually did (arbitra_multi_asset_ta_oscillator_fast_slow_divergence_mtf.py:723-726, start = min(len(frame), max(plan.holdout_start, warmup))): the replay begins at max(first evaluable bar, tracking_start), which is cheaper and confines a catastrophic trade to its own window -- but it DISCARDS any position open at that boundary and re-opens on the first pulse after it, so previously published signals, fills and exits can change. Position continuity across the boundary is the thing being traded away. The default is not switched automatically; the policy in force is emitted on every run.
reimplemented_logic.risk: A whole-history replay carries a position across the tracking boundary, so today's reported state depends on 2023 bars, and it reaches lifecycle states the bounded campaign never could. The concrete one is bankruptcy: SignalLifecycleEvaluator abandons the segment at a trade that clips to net -1.0 (signal_lifecycle.py:165) and skips the end_of_segment force-close (:174), so the whole tail is unevaluated. It cost XRPUSDT.ta_pvo.4h.opposite_signal 3,487 bars and 61 entry pulses, reported as a healthy flat cell.

reimplemented_logic.what: _frozen_decline_rule re-expresses each frozen evaluator's decline policy in order to decide the ONE pulse the frozen evaluator has not ruled on: the one on the newest completed bar, which its loop (range(start, end - 1)) never reaches. AtrBracketLifecycleEvaluator reads was_flat_at_signal at the top of the bar (rsi_fast_slow_divergence.py:584) and gates entry on it (:601), so it ignores every pulse while a position is open; SignalLifecycleEvaluator reverses on the opposite direction (signal_lifecycle.py:156-158) and re-enters after a side-specific long_exit/short_exit (:153-155, :168), so only a same-direction pulse with no explicit exit is declined.
reimplemented_logic.why: The state is decidable at the signal bar and the ledger is append-only. record_identity hashes {ledger_id, record_type, signal_id, identity_suffix} and signal_id hashes {registry_id, watch_id, direction, signal_bar_open_utc}; neither includes fill state, so a record written 'pending' on the tick the bar closed dedups away when the corrected one is produced and stays wrong forever. Measured before the fix: 192 of 536 signal records (35.8%) were pulses declined for position_already_open, each the newest bucket on exactly one tick of the 30-minute cadence, and XRPUSDT.ta_pvo.2h published a durable pending at 2026-07-30T20:05Z that three later runs could not correct.
reimplemented_logic.risk: A drifted rule would publish 'not_taken' for a pulse the frozen evaluator actually filled -- a false negative in an append-only ledger, which is strictly worse than the stale 'pending' it replaces.

ledger.identity_key: signal_id = sha256(canonical_json({registry_id, watch_id, direction, signal_bar_open_utc})); record_id = sha256(canonical_json({ledger_id, record_type, signal_id, identity_suffix}))

retention.ledger_policy: append-only; partitions are never rewritten, compacted or pruned
retention.partition_scheme: one file per UTC calendar month of the record's bar
retention.expected_records_per_month_basis: 360 trades across the 15 active cells over the 245-day retrospective confirmation window [2025-11-29, 2026-08-01) = 44.7 signal records per month, before fill and exit continuations. Base rate to read it against: that is the rate the SELECTED cells produced on the segment they were retained on but not selected on; it describes the past and forecasts nothing. Per the registry these cells are not established as distinguishable from search noise. XRPUSDT ta_pvo 2h alone contributes 86 of the 360.

divergence_armed.derivation: Read from the frozen outputs, not recomputed: the armed side is the LAST confirmation bar j from regular_divergence_events with state_bar - j <= max_event_age_bars and no qualified_entry_pulses entry on that side in [j, state_bar]. This mirrors qualified_entry_pulses' internal bullish_armed_at / bearish_armed_at, which the frozen function does not return.

parity_assertion.rule: For every completed bar: derived bullish armed AND fast > slow implies long_entry is True on that bar, and symmetrically for bearish/short. A failure means the derivation has drifted from the frozen state machine; the cell is forced to source_unavailable with reason parity_assertion_failed rather than publishing a signal.

fill_state_decidability.rule: A signal record may claim 'filled' only when the frozen lifecycle evaluator returned a trade whose signal bar IS this signal's bar. 'pending' means the frozen evaluator COULD still act on this pulse and the bar it would fill on has not appeared yet -- only ever the last completed bar, and only where the decline is not already decided. 'not_taken' means the frozen evaluator declined the pulse, and the reason says why. The presence of a next bar in the frame is NOT evidence that a position opened, and neither is the absence of one evidence that a fill is still possible: both frozen evaluators decline some pulses on facts that are fully known at the signal bar.
fill_state_decidability.residual_uncertainty: 'pending' remains a claim about the future in exactly one respect: both frozen evaluators execute at open(t+1), and that bar does not exist yet. Where the evaluator would act, the entry can still fail to happen if the next open is not finite and positive (signal_lifecycle.py:149, rsi_fast_slow_divergence.py:603), or -- on SignalLifecycleEvaluator only -- if the reversal's own closing trade clips to net -1.0, which latches bankrupt at signal_lifecycle.py:140 and breaks the loop at :165 before the entry is opened. Measured over the whole anchored history of all 15 active cells, 2,543 pulses had their outcome decided by the frozen evaluator and that second path occurred once (XRPUSDT.ta_pvo.4h.opposite_signal, signal bar 2024-12-27T12:00:00+00:00). Nothing else about a 'pending' record is unknown at write time.

final_bucket.rule: The FINAL bucket is provisional when its last observed child closes before the bucket's own clock close AND the same bucket-of-week (weekday, time-of-day) has historically been complete in at least 95% of at least 20 prior observations. The cell stays available and keeps reporting state; it publishes no NEW signal on that bucket, because a bucket the feed has not finished publishing produces a different oscillator reading from the one the market produced. Measured: dropping the last 30 minutes of the clock-closed SPY 2026-08-28 12:00-16:00 4h bucket -- a 15% volume shortfall -- moved the fast PVO leg 6.9 points.

'not_taken' means the frozen evaluator declined the pulse, and the reason says why. The presence of a next bar in the frame is NOT evidence that a position opened, and neither is the absence of one evidence that a fill is still possible: both frozen evaluators decline some pulses on facts that are fully known at the signal bar.
fill_state_decidability.residual_uncertainty: 'pending' remains a claim about the future in exactly one respect: both frozen evaluators execute at open(t+1), and that bar does not exist yet. Where the evaluator would act, the entry can still fail to happen if the next open is not finite and positive (signal_lifecycle.py:149, rsi_fast_slow_divergence.py:603), or -- on SignalLifecycleEvaluator only -- if the reversal's own closing trade clips to net -1.0, which latches bankrupt at signal_lifecycle.py:140 and breaks the loop at :165 before the entry is opened. Measured over the whole anchored history of all 15 active cells, 2,543 pulses had their outcome decided by the frozen evaluator and that second path occurred once (XRPUSDT.ta_pvo.4h.opposite_signal, signal bar 2024-12-27T12:00:00+00:00). Nothing else about a 'pending' record is unknown at write time.

final_bucket.rule: The FINAL bucket is provisional when its last observed child closes before the bucket's own clock close AND the same bucket-of-week (weekday, time-of-day) has historically been complete in at least 95% of at least 20 prior observations. The cell stays available and keeps reporting state; it publishes no NEW signal on that bucket, because a bucket the feed has not finished publishing produces a different oscillator reading from the one the market produced. Measured: dropping the last 30 minutes of the clock-closed SPY 2026-08-28 12:00-16:00 4h bucket -- a 15% volume shortfall -- moved the fast PVO leg 6.9 points.

known_limitations: The double-positive rate across the campaign (16/437 = 3.7%) exceeds the independence expectation (2.4%) only modestly; this set is NOT established as distinguishable from search noise.
Of 75 cells that passed holdout, only 21.3% stayed positive on confirmation, against a 14.2% marginal rate.
Cells are not independent: adjacent timeframes share signals, and ta_stochastic and ta_williams_r rows appear numerically identical in several cases.
No shifted-label or permutation null has been run against these survivors.
The retrospective confirmation window ends 2026-08-01, so tracking after that date is genuinely unseen data. That is the purpose of this registry.

divergence_armed.derivation: Read from the frozen outputs, not recomputed: the armed side is the LAST confirmation bar j from regular_divergence_events with state_bar - j <= max_event_age_bars and no qualified_entry_pulses entry on that side in [j, state_bar]. This mirrors qualified_entry_pulses' internal bullish_armed_at / bearish_armed_at, which the frozen function does not return.

parity_assertion.rule: For every completed bar: derived bullish armed AND fast > slow implies long_entry is True on that bar, and symmetrically for bearish/short. deferred.reason: Deferred by human decision. The OIL cells require Databento CL continuous futures with the contract-roll handling the frozen protocol mandates (protocol.frozen.json -> futures.roll_policy: "force flat and reset adapter/divergence/evaluator state"), implemented by RollResetAdapter and RollResetLifecycleEvaluator. The candle data exists (data/databento-futures/cl/1min/); the roll-reset evaluation path is what is missing. No adapter is instantiated and no signal is produced for these cells. Their warmup_bars_required values (156 and 124) are reproducible from the frozen adapter, so a later OIL build has a checkable target.

termination.frozen_source: integrations/signal_lifecycle.py:140 latches bankrupt, :165 breaks out of the bar loop, :174 skips the end_of_segment force-close
termination.detail: XRPUSDT.ta_pvo.4h.opposite_signal: the frozen SignalLifecycleEvaluator stopped at a bankrupt short signalled 2024-10-28T20:00:00+00:00: 0.5195 -> 2.1447 is a -3.1284 gross move, clipped by the frozen evaluator to net -1.0. It returned 36 trades and abandoned the segment. 3487 bars and 61 entry pulses after 2024-12-27T16:00:00+00:00 were NEVER evaluated. This cell is not flat and has no knowable position; it must not be presented as healthy. Resolving it is a human decision -- see replay_start_policy.

fill_state_decidability.rule: A signal record may claim 'filled' only when the frozen lifecycle evaluator returned a trade whose signal bar IS this signal's bar. 'pending' means the frozen evaluator COULD still act on this pulse and the bar it would fill on has not appeared yet -- only ever the last completed bar, and only where the decline is not already decided. 'not_taken' means the frozen evaluator declined the pulse, and the reason says why. The presence of a next bar in the frame is NOT evidence that a position opened, and neither is the absence of one evidence that a fill is still possible: both frozen evaluators decline some pulses on facts that are fully known at the signal bar.
fill_state_decidability.residual_uncertainty: 'pending' remains a claim about the future in exactly one respect: both frozen evaluators execute at open(t+1), and that bar does not exist yet. Where the evaluator would act, the entry can still fail to happen if the next open is not finite and positive (signal_lifecycle.py:149, rsi_fast_slow_divergence.py:603), or -- on SignalLifecycleEvaluator only -- if the reversal's own closing trade clips to net -1.0, which latches bankrupt at signal_lifecycle.py:140 and breaks the loop at :165 before the entry is opened. Measured over the whole anchored history of all 15 active cells, 2,543 pulses had their outcome decided by the frozen evaluator and that second path occurred once (XRPUSDT.ta_pvo.4h.opposite_signal, signal bar 2024-12-27T12:00:00+00:00). Nothing else about a 'pending' record is unknown at write time.

final_bucket.rule: The FINAL bucket is provisional when its last observed child closes before the bucket's own clock close AND the same bucket-of-week (weekday, time-of-day) has historically been complete in at least 95% of at least 20 prior observations. The cell stays available and keeps reporting state; it publishes no NEW signal on that bucket, because a bucket the feed has not finished publishing produces a different oscillator reading from the one the market produced. Measured: dropping the last 30 minutes of the clock-closed SPY 2026-08-28 12:00-16:00 4h bucket -- a 15% volume shortfall -- moved the fast PVO leg 6.9 points.

known_limitations: The double-positive rate across the campaign (16/437 = 3.7%) exceeds the independence expectation (2.4%) only modestly; this set is NOT established as distinguishable from search noise.
Of 75 cells that passed holdout, only 21.3% stayed positive on confirmation, against a 14.2% marginal rate.
Cells are not independent: adjacent timeframes share signals, and ta_stochastic and ta_williams_r rows appear numerically identical in several cases.
No shifted-label or permutation null has been run against these survivors.
The retrospective confirmation window ends 2026-08-01, so tracking after that date is genuinely unseen data. That is the purpose of this registry.
